newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore finance chief calls for bank alliances.
newsitem.headline: Singapore finance chief calls for bank alliances.

text.p: Forging alliances is the best way for Asian banks to face the competitive pressures that will follow the liberalisation of the region's financial markets, Singapore Finance Minister Richard Hu said on Thursday.
"They could participate more actively in each other's financial markets either through strategic alliances or embarking on joint venture projects," he told a conference on project financing.

"Such efforts will help to sharpen the competitive edge of the Asian banks to prepare them for the eventual opening up of the global financial markets under the World Trade Organisation (WTO)," Hu said.
He said collaboration would help maximise comparative strengths of the region's banks.

Singapore Prime Minster Goh Chok Tong offered similar views during an official visit to Thailand this week, encouraging Singapore banks to buy into licenced Thai finance houses to acquire Thai banking licences, the Straits Times newspaper said.
Goh said the Thai government would be happy to consider granting full licences to Singapore banks which already have Bangkok International Banking facility (BIBF) licences.
Malaysia's Bank Negara has also encouraged mergers between regional banks to combat international competition.

"The issue here is that we want to have a core of sizeable financial institutions to be able to operate and compete in a more liberalised environment," Bank Negara governor Datuk Ahmad Mohammad Don said in March, according to the Straits Times.
